quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I've just signed a three-year contract with them.'
options: He announced he had just signed a three-year contract with them.
He announced he has just signed a three-year contract with them.
He announced he had just been signing a three-year contract with them.
quests.correctAnswer: He announced he had just signed a three-year contract with them.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I've just signed a three-year contract with them.'
quests.hint: Present perfect → past perfect. 'Just' stays in position. Reporting verb: 'announced'.
quests.explanation: 'Have just signed' → 'had just signed'. 'Announced' suits a significant personal achievement.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Doesn't this prove that the system needs improvement?'
options: She asked whether that didn't prove the system needed improvement.
She asked doesn't this prove that the system needs improvement.
She asked whether this doesn't prove that the system needed improvement.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked whether that didn't prove the system needed improvement.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Doesn't this prove that the system needs improvement?'
quests.hint: Negative question: 'doesn't prove' → 'didn't prove'. 'This' → 'that'. 'Needs' → 'needed'. Use 'whether'.
quests.explanation: Three shifts: 'doesn't prove' → 'didn't prove', 'this' → 'that', 'needs' → 'needed'. Use 'whether' and statement order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The communication workshop said, 'Listen actively and avoid interrupting the speaker.'
options: The communication workshop instructed participants to listen actively and avoid interrupting the speaker.
The communication workshop instructed participants to listen actively and to avoid to interrupt the speaker.
The communication workshop said listen actively and avoid interrupting the speaker.
quests.correctAnswer: The communication workshop instructed participants to listen actively and avoid interrupting the speaker.
quests.sentence: The communication workshop said, 'Listen actively and avoid interrupting the speaker.'
quests.hint: 'Listen' and 'avoid interrupting': 'told + to + listen and avoid + -ing'. Do not use 'to' before 'interrupt' after 'avoid'.
quests.explanation: 'Avoid' is followed by the gerund (-ing), not the infinitive. 'Avoid interrupting' is correct; 'avoid to interrupt' is wrong.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The manager said, 'The bonus will be paid by the end of the month.'
options: The manager said the bonus would be paid by the end of the month.
The manager said the bonus will be paid by the end of the month.
The manager said the bonus would have been paid by the end of the month.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager said the bonus would be paid by the end of the month.
quests.sentence: The manager said, 'The bonus will be paid by the end of the month.'
quests.hint: 'Will be paid' → 'would be paid'. Future passive → conditional passive.
quests.explanation: Future passive 'will be paid' shifts to conditional passive 'would be paid' in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The engineer was asked, 'What do you believe caused the equipment failure?'
options: The engineer was asked what she believed had caused the equipment failure.
The engineer was asked what she believed caused the equipment failure.
The engineer was asked what does she believe caused the equipment failure.
quests.correctAnswer: The engineer was asked what she believed had caused the equipment failure.
quests.sentence: The engineer was asked, 'What do you believe caused the equipment failure?'
quests.hint: 'Do believe' → 'believed'. Embedded 'caused' → 'had caused'. 'You' → 'she'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: Two shifts: 'believe' → 'believed' and 'caused' → 'had caused'. The embedded verb in reported questions also shifts.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The account manager said, 'Take detailed notes during the client meetings.'
options: The account manager told the team to take detailed notes during the client meetings.
The account manager told taking detailed notes during client meetings.
The account manager said take detailed notes during the client meetings.
quests.correctAnswer: The account manager told the team to take detailed notes during the client meetings.
quests.sentence: The account manager said, 'Take detailed notes during the client meetings.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'told + team + to + take'.
quests.explanation: 'Take' is an imperative → 'told the team to take detailed notes during the client meetings'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I'm afraid the news isn't what we were hoping for.'
options: She said she was afraid the news wasn't what they had been hoping for.
She said she's afraid the news isn't what they were hoping for.
She said she was afraid the news wasn't what they were hoping for.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she was afraid the news wasn't what they had been hoping for.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I'm afraid the news isn't what we were hoping for.'
quests.hint: 'Am afraid' → 'was afraid'. 'Isn't' → 'wasn't'. 'Were hoping' → 'had been hoping'. 'We' → 'they'.
quests.explanation: Three tense shifts: 'am afraid' → 'was afraid', 'isn't' → 'wasn't', and 'were hoping' → 'had been hoping'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The chairman asked, 'Were there any objections to the proposed merger?'
options: The chairman asked whether there had been any objections to the proposed merger.
The chairman asked whether there were any objections to the proposed merger.
The chairman asked were there any objections to the proposed merger.
quests.correctAnswer: The chairman asked whether there had been any objections to the proposed merger.
quests.sentence: The chairman asked, 'Were there any objections to the proposed merger?'
quests.hint: 'Were there' → 'there had been'. Use 'whether' and statement order.
quests.explanation: Past simple 'were there' shifts to past perfect 'there had been'. Use 'whether' for yes/no questions.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The treasurer said, 'Document all expenses and keep your receipts.'
options: The treasurer told members to document all expenses and keep their receipts.
The treasurer told members to document all expenses and keep your receipts.
The treasurer said document all expenses and keep your receipts.
quests.correctAnswer: The treasurer told members to document all expenses and keep their receipts.
quests.sentence: The treasurer said, 'Document all expenses and keep your receipts.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: 'told + members + to + document... and keep'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: Two imperatives → 'told members to document all expenses and keep their receipts'. 'Your receipts' → 'their receipts'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The historian wrote, 'Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.'
options: The historian wrote that Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.
The historian wrote that Shakespeare had been born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.
The historian wrote that Shakespeare is born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.
quests.correctAnswer: The historian wrote that Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.
quests.sentence: The historian wrote, 'Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.'
quests.hint: Historical facts with specific dates stay in past simple. They do not shift to past perfect.
quests.explanation: Historical events reported in past simple ('was born') stay in past simple when reported. They do not shift to past perfect.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Who has been managing the account in my absence?'
options: She asked who had been managing the account in her absence.
She asked who has been managing the account in her absence.
She asked who had managed the account in her absence.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked who had been managing the account in her absence.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Who has been managing the account in my absence?'
quests.hint: 'Has been managing' → 'had been managing'. 'My' → 'her'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Has been managing' (present perfect continuous) → 'had been managing'. 'My absence' → 'her absence'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The networking guide said, 'Build strong relationships with your colleagues and clients.'
options: The networking guide advised professionals to build strong relationships with their colleagues and clients.
The networking guide advised to build strong relationships with your colleagues and clients.
The networking guide said building strong relationships with colleagues and clients.
quests.correctAnswer: The networking guide advised professionals to build strong relationships with their colleagues and clients.
quests.sentence: The networking guide said, 'Build strong relationships with your colleagues and clients.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'advised + professionals + to + build'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: 'Build' is an imperative → 'advised professionals to build strong relationships'. 'Your colleagues' → 'their colleagues'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I wouldn't say the presentation was perfect.'
options: She said she wouldn't say the presentation had been perfect.
She said she wouldn't say the presentation was perfect.
She said she wouldn't have said the presentation had been perfect.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she wouldn't say the presentation had been perfect.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I wouldn't say the presentation was perfect.'
quests.hint: 'Wouldn't say' stays. 'Was perfect' → 'had been perfect'. 'I' → 'she'.
quests.explanation: 'Wouldn't say' does not shift further. 'Was perfect' shifts to 'had been perfect'. 'I' → 'she'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The client asked, 'How many months has the project been delayed?'
options: The client asked how many months the project had been delayed.
The client asked how many months has the project been delayed.
The client asked how many months the project was delayed.
quests.correctAnswer: The client asked how many months the project had been delayed.
quests.sentence: The client asked, 'How many months has the project been delayed?'
quests.hint: 'Has been delayed' → 'had been delayed'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: Present perfect passive 'has been delayed' shifts to past perfect passive 'had been delayed'. Use statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The feedback session said, 'Be transparent about your limitations.'
options: The feedback session encouraged candidates to be transparent about their limitations.
The feedback session encouraged candidates to be transparent about your limitations.
The feedback session said be transparent about your limitations.
quests.correctAnswer: The feedback session encouraged candidates to be transparent about their limitations.
quests.sentence: The feedback session said, 'Be transparent about your limitations.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'encouraged + candidates + to + be transparent'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: 'Be transparent' is an imperative → 'encouraged candidates to be transparent about their limitations'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I'll have the report ready by Thursday morning.'
options: She promised she would have the report ready by Thursday morning.
She promised she will have the report ready by Thursday morning.
She promised the report would be ready by Thursday morning.
quests.correctAnswer: She promised she would have the report ready by Thursday morning.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I'll have the report ready by Thursday morning.'
quests.hint: 'Will have' → 'would have'. Reporting verb: 'promised'. Subject stays 'she'.
quests.explanation: 'Will have the report ready' → 'would have the report ready'. 'Promised' expresses a commitment. The subject 'she' must be retained.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The professor asked, 'What led you to pursue a career in medicine?'
options: The professor asked what had led me to pursue a career in medicine.
The professor asked what led me to pursue a career in medicine.
The professor asked what had led you to pursue a career in medicine.
quests.correctAnswer: The professor asked what had led me to pursue a career in medicine.
quests.sentence: The professor asked, 'What led you to pursue a career in medicine?'
quests.hint: 'Led' → 'had led'. 'You' → 'me'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: Past simple 'led' shifts to past perfect 'had led'. 'You' → 'me'. Use statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The journalism tutor said, 'Avoid making assumptions - always verify the facts.'
options: The journalism tutor told students to avoid making assumptions and always verify the facts.
The journalism tutor told students avoiding making assumptions and always to verify the facts.
The journalism tutor said avoid making assumptions - always verify the facts.
quests.correctAnswer: The journalism tutor told students to avoid making assumptions and always verify the facts.
quests.sentence: The journalism tutor said, 'Avoid making assumptions - always verify the facts.'
quests.hint: 'Avoid making' (imperative + gerund) + 'verify' (imperative). Use 'told + to + avoid making and verify'.
quests.explanation: 'Avoid making' → 'to avoid making'. 'Verify' → 'verify' (parallel structure after 'and'). 'Avoiding making... and always to verify' is incorrect.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'She wishes she hadn't said that.'
options: He said she wished she hadn't said that.
He said she wishes she hadn't said that.
He said she wished she hadn't been saying that.
quests.correctAnswer: He said she wished she hadn't said that.
quests.sentence: He said, 'She wishes she hadn't said that.'
quests.hint: 'Wishes' → 'wished'. 'Hadn't said' stays (already past perfect). 'She' stays.
quests.explanation: 'Wishes' → 'wished'. 'Hadn't said' is already past perfect - it cannot shift further. 'She' stays as the subject.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Is this the most efficient approach available?'
options: She asked whether that was the most efficient approach available.
She asked is this the most efficient approach available.
She asked whether this was the most efficient approach available.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked whether that was the most efficient approach available.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Is this the most efficient approach available?'
quests.hint: 'Is' → 'was'. 'This' → 'that'. Use 'whether' and statement order.
quests.explanation: Two shifts: 'is' → 'was' and 'this' → 'that'. Use 'whether' for yes/no questions. Statement word order: 'whether that was'.

quests.explanation: 'Develop' is an imperative → 'encouraged students to develop a habit of reviewing their work critically'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The global HR guide said, 'Be mindful of cultural differences when working internationally.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I'm confident we can find a solution that works for everyone.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'Has there been any progress on the investigation?'

He asked was there any progress on the investigation.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The career advisor said, 'Never underestimate the importance of communication skills.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The team leader said, 'We've been making great progress over the last few months.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The employee asked, 'What criteria are used to assess performance?'

quests.sentence: The employee asked, 'What criteria are used to assess performance?'
quests.hint: 'Are used' → 'were used'. Statement order. General process: no over-shift to past perfect.
quests.explanation: 'Are used' (present passive) → 'were used' (past passive). This is a general process question, so 'had been used' would be an over-shift.
